cases.modeling_form: sequence_var route with external_call distance evaluator

constraints: sequence_var represents a permutation, so no separate all-different constraint is required
optagent_modeling.data_mapping: Read TSPLIB coordinates or explicit distances and implement the documented TSPLIB distance metric in a callback.
decision_variables: one sequence_var tour of size 52; the sequence is the city visit order
optagent_modeling.external_callback: route_cost(ctx) reads ctx.value(tour), sums consecutive arc costs, and adds the return-to-start arc.

cases.problem_description: TSPLIB symmetric TSP instance berlin52: find the shortest Hamiltonian cycle over 52 cities using the instance distance metric. The benchmark is a blackbox sequence optimization case with a published optimal tour length.

recommended_evaluation.primary_route: solve(..., strategy=GaConfig/TabuConfig/AlnsConfig); exact route only for small diagnostic comparisons

reference.notes: TSPLIB STSP page states all symmetric TSP instances are solved to optimality.

cases.modeling_form: sequence_var assignment permutation with external_call quadratic cost evaluator

constraints: sequence_var enforces a one-to-one facility-location assignment
optagent_modeling.data_mapping: Read QAPLIB flow and distance matrices.
decision_variables: one sequence_var assignment of size 12; assignment[i] is the location chosen for facility i
optagent_modeling.external_callback: qap_cost(ctx) computes sum(flow[i][j] * distance[assignment[i]][assignment[j]]) over all facility pairs.

cases.problem_description: QAPLIB quadratic assignment instance chr12a: assign 12 facilities to 12 locations. The cost is the sum of flow between facility pairs multiplied by distance between assigned locations. This is a permutation blackbox benchmark with a published optimum.

recommended_evaluation.primary_route: solve(..., strategy=GaConfig/TabuConfig/AlnsConfig); not a natural pure MILP benchmark for OptAgent strategies

cases.modeling_form: MPS/MP rows and columns for exact backend evaluation

constraints: one linear constraint per MPS row using the parsed row sense and right-hand side
optagent_modeling.data_mapping: Load the MPS instance through the benchmark MPS/MP loader and preserve row sense, bounds, integrality, and objective coefficients.
decision_variables: bool_var for binary columns
int_var for general integer columns
float_var for continuous columns
optagent_modeling.objective: builder.minimize(parsed_linear_objective, name='mip_objective') unless the source sense states maximize

deferred_candidates.reason: Important for steel-like sequencing, but first-class catalog inclusion should wait for a stable machine-readable lower/upper-bound source and a dedicated parser.
Requires optional interval or machine-choice modeling support before it is a natural OptAgent benchmark.
Useful sequence/set benchmark, but requires richer route/list-of-routes modeling than the current single sequence_var examples.

families.cumulative_resource_scheduling: PSPLIB RCPSP instances mapped to interval/precedence/cumulative.
families.exact_linear_mip: MIPLIB rows/columns mapped to MP/MPS exact backend evaluation.
families.interval_job_shop: JSPLIB job-shop instances mapped to interval/no_overlap/precedence.
families.sequence_blackbox_tsp: TSPLIB TSP instances mapped to sequence_var plus external distance callback.
families.sequence_quadratic_assignment: QAPLIB instances mapped to sequence_var plus quadratic external callback.

objective: Benchmark OptAgent against problem families that match current modeling primitives. Pure MILP/MPS remains a dedicated exact-backend sub-benchmark.

recommended_directory_structure.purpose: Human entrypoint for benchmark scope, source policy, and execution workflow.
Versioned source-of-truth catalogs with external references, selected cases, and modeling declarations.
Family-specific case manifests, parser adapters, and OptAgent model builders.
Reusable loaders that fetch or read public benchmark formats and normalize data records.
OptAgent ModelBuilder/program construction for each benchmark family.
Common exact and strategy benchmark runners. They consume catalog ids and write run artifacts.
Ignored local cache for downloaded public instances. Keep raw external data out of commits unless explicitly vendored.
Rendered catalog snapshots used in documentation and review.
Local or CI run artifacts: config, JSONL events, result JSON, and summary Markdown.
Curated comparison reports derived from run artifacts.

source_policy: Reference objectives and bounds are taken from public benchmark sources; local solve runs are never used as ground truth.

tiers.calibration: Medium cases for strategy and exact backend regression.
tiers.full: Larger or harder cases for offline performance assessment.
tiers.smoke: Small cases for parser/modeling/solver route checks.
